title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
claim: Photosensitizer-modified Ce6 metal–organic layers drive HER by a dual excitation sequence in which the reduced Ru or Ir ligand reduces Ce(IV) to Ce(III), and spin-allowed 4f→5d excitation of Ce(III) then reduces protons.
explanation: Ce6–BTB MOLs functionalized with MBA-Ru or MBA-Ir ligands evolved H2 9.3- and 8.7-fold faster than the corresponding homogeneous systems. The review attributes this to the stability and photoactivity of the Ce6 node plus the sensitizer, and describes BIH reduction of excited Ru(II), electron transfer to Ce(IV), and reoxidation of photoexcited Ce(III) during H+ reduction.
scope: Ce6(μ3-O)4(μ3-OH)4 cluster MOLs with Ru or Ir photosensitizing ligands.
conditions: UV–vis 350–700 nm; BIH; MeCN:AcOH (40:1); Ce6–BTB–Ir TON 1357 in Table 1.
caveats: The dual-path mechanism is reported for these Ce(IV/III) MOLs and is not claimed for redox-inert lanthanides.
